This article compares the age distribution of operated patients across [[danmark|Danmark]], its five regions, and individual hospitals for the period 01/09/2022 to 31/08/2023. Understanding these demographics is critical for healthcare resource allocation, as age heavily influences surgical complexity, recovery times, and postoperative care needs. The data, drawn from the AKDB 2023 and 2024 reports, tracks patient counts, percentages, quartiles, medians, and means to highlight demographic burdens and specialized care distribution across the country.

### Leaders and Trailers
Nationally, the median age of operated patients was 70.00 years, with a mean age of 65.42 in the 2023 report [^src1] and 65.46 in the 2024 report [^src2]. [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] consistently recorded the youngest patient population, posting the lowest mean age of 51.22 years in both publications [^src1] [^src2]. Conversely, the oldest patient populations were found at smaller or specialized units. In the 2023 report, [[nykoebing-f-sygehus|Nykøbing F Sygehus]] recorded the highest mean age of 87.50 years, though this was based on a negligible sample size representing just 0.3% of the regional total [^src1]. Among major hospitals listed in the 2024 report, [[regionshospital-nordjylland|Regionshospital Nordjylland]] had the highest mean age at 70.71 years [^src2].

### Outliers
[[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] stands out as a significant statistical outlier. While the national first quartile (Q1) is 56.00 years, Rigshospitalet's Q1 is 38.00 years, indicating that at least 25% of its surgical patients are under 38 [^src1] [^src2]. This likely reflects its role as a national center for specialized, trauma, and pediatric surgeries. Similarly, [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] exhibits a high third quartile (Q3) of 82.00 years despite having a mean age (64.48) close to the national average, suggesting a distinct bimodal or heavily right-skewed age distribution on the island [^src1] [^src2].

### Data Revisions vs. Temporal Trends
Because both the 2023 and 2024 source documents report on the exact same timeframe (01/09/2022 – 31/08/2023), there are no chronological trends to analyze. Instead, the differences between the two tables represent data revisions, late registrations, or methodological updates between publication years. For instance, the total national count of operated patients was revised upward from 3,718 [^src1] to 3,745 [^src2]. All five regions saw slight increases in their total counts (e.g., [[sjaelland-region-i-alt|Sjælland Region i alt]] grew from 587 to 595) [^src1] [^src2]. Notably, [[nykoebing-f-sygehus|Nykøbing F Sygehus]] appears in the 2023 data but is entirely absent from the 2024 table, suggesting its cases may have been reassigned, suppressed for privacy due to low counts, or merged into another entity like [[sjaellands-universitetshospital|Sjællands Universitetshospital]] [^src1] [^src2].
